extracted.intended_audience: early-career faculty researchers and institutional nominators at invited institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Selection criteria and eligibility guidance for the Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering, used by nominators and candidates to understand who is eligible and how applications are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Stage (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be faculty members engaged in research in the natural and physical sciences or engineering and must be within the first three years of their faculty careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility cutoff — applicants must be early-career faculty (first three years) and actively engaged in relevant research disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Focus / Disciplines Considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible research disciplines include Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, Astronomy, Computer science, Earth science, Ocean science, and all branches of engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship is targeted at basic and fundamental research across these natural and physical sciences and engineering fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical research; research associated with large national facilities (accelerators, space stations); applied research of direct relevance to national security; and social sciences are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals or candidates whose work falls primarily in these excluded areas are not appropriate for the Fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Approach: Innovative individual research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation emphasizes support for innovative individual research that involves the Fellows, their students, and junior colleagues, rather than extensions or components of large-scale, ongoing research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High value is placed on independent, creative projects led by the candidate and providing training/collaboration opportunities for trainees and junior colleagues; work that is merely a component of a large program is less favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation letters (weighty criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation letters are one of the most important evaluation criteria; recommenders who are themselves Packard Fellows or mentored Packard Fellows are highly regarded as letter writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, credible endorsements (especially from Packard Fellows or those who have mentored them) carry substantial weight in the selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance / impact of research
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected importance and impact of the candidate's research is one of the most important evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for work that addresses significant problems and has the potential for substantial scientific or engineering impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication track record is important to be recognized and labeled as an expert in a field for a specific body of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demonstrable record of influential publications helps establish the candidate's expertise and standing in their area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous funding and awards (positive signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having previous funding and/or awards can be perceived as a positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior recognition and support may strengthen a candidate's profile, though they are not stated as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-taking and originality preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-taking and originality are valued over incremental work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that are bold, novel, and potentially high-reward are favored relative to safe, incremental extensions of existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Process (panel & recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Packard Fellowships Advisory Panel — a group of 12 internationally recognized scientists and engineers — evaluates the nominations and recommends Fellows for approval by the Packard Foundation Board of Trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is peer-reviewed by a small expert panel whose recommendations are subject to Board approval; applicants/nominators should be aware the process is competitive and externally evaluated.
